stem.en: What made the caves, sinkholes and underground rivers of a limestone hill?

feedback.en: Yes. All of them come from water dissolving limestone.

text.en: Sea waves that once beat against the hill

feedback.en: Waves cut sea caves at the coast. These form far from any shore.

text.en: Wind carrying sand through the rock

feedback.en: Wind cannot reach the inside of solid rock.

text.en: Glacier ice that pushed through the hill

feedback.en: Ice carves valleys on the surface, not passages inside limestone.

explanation.en: Rain becomes a weak acid and dissolves limestone along its cracks. This opens caves and passages, and roofs that fall in make sinkholes. Geologists call these landforms karst topography.

hints.en: Which agent can reach inside solid rock?
